title: Should You Buy Uber Stock Before the Huge Investor Update?
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc previews Uber's 4 Nov earnings and answers whether to buy beforehand: for new buyers, yes — a great buy before earnings; for existing holders, wait until after the print, since they already hold the upside. Uber is down 19% year to date in 2026 as driverless-car risk weighs on the stock. The operating picture is strong: gross bookings +24% to $58B, revenue +12% to $14.2B, operating income +30% to $1.9B, operating cash flow $2.9B, and over 28M monthly active platform customers (+16%). The risk is Waymo increasingly going it alone rather than partnering with Uber, plus a possible Tesla-SpaceX merger giving Tesla far more capital for its robotaxi network; regulation in the US and EU will be slow and cautious, while China moves faster. He argues Uber can counter by buying its own fleet cheaply amid a global glut of auto manufacturing capacity (130-135M units versus ~100M sold) and licensing driverless technology. Other tickers discussed: Tesla (overpromised on robotaxis again in 2026), Waymo (Alphabet's unit, unnamed as a ticker), Rivian and Lucid (fleet partners). Calls made: UBER — CONDITIONAL_BUY, fair value $122 versus $66 market (buy-side stance kept; was BUY 8 Oct, no flip); he ranks it a top-10 stock to buy and owns it but will not add before earnings.

Driverless risk (Waymo going solo, a possible Tesla/SpaceX merger) overhangs an otherwise growing business.
calls.bull_case: Gross bookings +24% to $58B, operating income +30% to $1.9B, cheapest-ever forward PE of 15, and huge global vehicle overcapacity it could buy into for its own fleet.
calls.bear_case: Waymo partnership fraying, Tesla robotaxi capital threat, and unresolved regulation/insurance questions; he expects the overhang to get worse before it gets better.
